F2_GWT_ADAPTIVE_RECURRENCE.result: Across authored heterogeneous synthetic regimes, pressure/trend adaptive recurrence matched fixed12 success (~60.67%) with ~47.1% fewer recurrence steps and higher cost-adjusted utility. This supports testing a controller basis combining unresolved pressure, multi-step marginal gain, cost, instability, budget, regime identity and provenance; GWT focus may inform but must not itself decide recurrence.
F2_GWT_ADAPTIVE_RECURRENCE.boundary: No evidence yet shows GWT focus has independent causal value or that recurrence-count savings become Ubuntu wall-clock savings.
counterhypotheses: ordinary persistent event-driven scheduling may be sufficient
routing overhead may erase compute savings
synthetic advantage may be authored-regime artifact
adaptive routing may shallow-halt on hard cases
one global controller may be sufficient

F3_ADAPTIVE_LESION_RESCUE_CONFOUND.result: Lesion/rescue is history-dependent in adaptive systems: online plasticity can compensate during the measurement interval, while mechanism-only rescue after compensation can fail to restore the original state. Emergence/causal tests must bind plasticity mode, measurement delay/window, learner-state lineage, compensation gain, rescue mode and common-snapshot counterfactual branches.
F3_ADAPTIVE_LESION_RESCUE_CONFOUND.boundary: This proves only that the confound is possible in a simple adaptive redundant model; it does not establish FRANK magnitude, timescale or mechanism.
F3_ADAPTIVE_LESION_RESCUE_CONFOUND.counterhypothesis: Frozen-learning acute interventions may remain sufficient for specific causal estimands if adaptation is explicitly excluded from the test window.
